solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Admission, in case dodgy Conservative succeeded

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and crooked, so these letters cannot be trusted to stay in order

parts.note: taken as written
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
s. is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A crooked Tory gets into office, and someone admits it, in case anyone asks.
explanation.walkthrough: The C and S join CASE before the shuffle, giving six letters to rearrange into ACCESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaining admission somewhere means being granted entry, the right of getting in.

clue.text: see 21dn.
The Sun's Eye-bashing evidence?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that shines brightly
second meaning: a black eye left by a punch

explanation.surface: The Sun tabloid runs a story attacking Private Eye and calls it proof.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes it look like the newspaper; it is the star in the sky. Eye-bashing is literal: a black eye is slang for a shiner.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun gives off light, so it shines; a bruised eye socket after a punch is called this in slang.

clue.text: Obscure charge involving U-turning idiots

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to indict is to formally charge with a crime

indicators.note: a U-turn sends you back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: nits is slang for fools

explanation.surface: A vague accusation is brought against fools who keep changing their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: Nits is everyday British slang for idiots, borrowed from the louse eggs; 'charge' here is the legal sense, not a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure as an adjective means hard to make out or unclear, the same as blurred and vague.

clue.text: Activist got at IRA's duplicity

indicators.note: duplicity is double-dealing deceit, so the letters are not what they seem and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A campaigner was got at by the IRA's double-dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The IRA is the Irish Republican Army; here its letters are just raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist who stirs up public feeling for a political cause is called a rabble-rousing stirrer of this kind.

clue.text: Nut-cracking the French way isn't right

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective: what isn't right is untrue

indicators.note: something cracking breaks open, so its letters come apart and reform

parts.note: the three letters broken up and rearranged
rue is French for street, a way

explanation.surface: Cracking nuts in the French manner is somehow wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins the fodder to its indicator so the surface reads as one activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement that is not correct is false, which is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: One who sets young Conservative loutish leaders breaking the law

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece enters another

parts.note: the law is slang for the police, the cops
Y is the abbreviation for young
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man who stirs up young Tory yobs into breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the setter's own pseudonym, so the definition is self-referential: he sets this very puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclops is the pen name of the compiler of Private Eye's crossword, so he is the puzzle setter.

clue.text: Sound of heavy smokers' chests?

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: heavy smokers are people who cough a lot

explanation.surface: The rattling noise of a chain-smoker's lungs.
explanation.walkthrough: Chests looks like ribcages to go with smokers; it means strongboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes for keeping money or valuables, a kind of locked chest.

clue.text: Bah! Bats variant for a day

indicators.note: a variant is a different version, so the letters appear in another form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble about a different species of bat, fit for a whole day.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats might be the animal or 'crazy'; here it simply supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest and worship, Saturday or Sunday depending on religion.

clue.text: Mitt ("good 'un!") offers protection for many Americans

parts.note: mitt is slang for hand
G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mitt Romney approves, saying a gun keeps Americans safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Mitt reads as Mitt Romney, the American politician, but it is slang for a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Many Americans keep a pistol for self-defence, so the weapon is described as their protection.

clue.text: China expels Republican 'devil'

indicators.note: to expel is to throw out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a friend
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Beijing throws out an American politician branded a devil.
explanation.walkthrough: China looks like the country; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an evil spirit or demon, the same thing as a devil.

clue.text: Tennis bra snapped — slid down in childish play

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a synonym

indicators.note: something snapped is broken, so its letters fall apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports bra breaks during a tennis match and slips down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: children famously slide down the handrail of a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: The handrail running alongside a staircase is what children ride down for fun.

clue.text: Failing to tax office furniture

parts.note: what fails to tax you is not taxing, that is, not difficult
the chair is an office, the post of chairperson

explanation.surface: Someone neglects to pay the tax due on their office desks and chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office furniture' wants to be read together as the definition; 'office' belongs to the wordplay, and tax means strain, not levy.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large comfortable upholstered armchair, a piece of household seating.

clue.text: Prisoner fines so wrong — may be given to priest

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place and must be put right

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jailed man thinks his fines are unjust and might take his complaint to a chaplain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes rather than names: a Catholic tells sins to a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: In confession a penitent tells their sins to a priest, so it is something offered to a cleric.

clue.text: Tax perverted sex article

indicators.note: to pervert is literally to turn the wrong way round

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal or sex
the definite article

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style story about levying duty on a kinky magazine piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Perverted sounds like a comment on the sex, but its root meaning is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a levy of one tenth of produce or income paid to support the church.

clue.text: A certain position, in which she playfully grabs orifice

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it, so one piece holds another
playing about with letters jumbles their order

parts.note: taken as written
a vent is an opening or orifice

explanation.surface: A saucy description of a sexual position in which she grabs something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'position' is a place in a ranking, not a sexual one; the smutty surface is typical of Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventh names one particular place in an order or ranking, so it is a specific position.

clue.text: Voter, um, is turned with hard drink

indicators.note: something turned over is upset and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hesitant voter is won over with the help of strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard drink reads as one phrase meaning spirits; 'hard' is the H and the definition is just 'drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, an alcoholic beverage used in martinis.

clue.text: A large figure under-performing in high definition

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: HD is the standard abbreviation for high definition

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on an act, so the letters take on a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plus-size star doing poorly in a high-definition broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under-performing' looks like a single word; the hyphen hides fodder plus indicator. A large figure sounds like a big person, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred is a sizeable round number, so it is a big figure in the numeric sense.

clue.text: Collector sporting more impressive erection (oxygen-enriched)

indicators.note: something enriched has had an extra ingredient added inside it

parts.note: a more impressive erection is a firmer one
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A collector boasting about an impressive, oxygen-boosted erection.
explanation.walkthrough: Erection could be a building, but this is Private Eye smut: the comparative of hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder amasses and stores things obsessively, so is a compulsive accumulator of objects.

clue.text: Ruin poor oldies parking at the centre

indicators.note: something at the centre sits in the middle, surrounded by the rest
poor means in bad shape, so the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Parking charges in the town centre are ruining hard-up pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' looks like a noun in the surface but works as a verb, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder or strip something of its value, to wreck or spoil it.

clue.text: (&23dn.) Cry for help expressed in this version of some credo?

definitions.text: Cry for help expressed in this

indicators.note: a version is the same material told another way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A desperate prayer for rescue, spoken in a form of some creed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry for help is SOS, famously sent in dots and dashes; credo suggests religion but just gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The distress signal SOS is classically transmitted as three dots, three dashes, three dots in telegraphy.

clue.text: President Biden ultimately follows Marco about

indicators.note: about can mean round and around, so the letters are turned about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the name

explanation.surface: The US president ends up trailing Marco Rubio around.
explanation.walkthrough: With Biden in the clue, 'President' wants to be him; it is the French president.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is the head of state of France, elected its president in 2017.

clue.text: Our bolshie Dave joins with Bill (Private Eye), whom many fellow rebels claimed to be

definitions.text: whom many fellow rebels claimed to be

parts.note: Dave Spart is Private Eye's spoof hard-left columnist
AC, short for account, is a bill
the magazine speaking of itself is us

explanation.surface: A Private Eye in-joke: the magazine's leftie columnist teams up with someone called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' signals a Private Eye character. In the film Spartacus, captured rebel slaves each stand and say 'I'm Spartacus' to shield him.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus led a slave revolt against Rome; in the famous film scene every captured comrade claims his identity.

clue.text: One revealing broadcaster takes heroin

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

parts.note: to broadcast is to scatter seed, so a sower is a broadcaster
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A TV presenter is exposed as a heroin user.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcaster suggests TV or radio; its older sense is a farmer scattering seed by hand. The definition reads the answer as show-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows something displays or exposes it, so the one doing the exposing fits.

clue.text: (& 2dn.) Ailment making you green and frigid

parts.note: a village green is shared land owned by the community, and the word for such land also means ordinary or widespread
frigid means icy or freezing, the opposite of hot

explanation.surface: An illness that leaves you looking green and shivering.
explanation.walkthrough: Green sounds like sickly colouring; it is a village green, an area of common land.
explanation.definitionFit: The common cold is a widespread viral infection of the nose and throat, a minor illness.

clue.text: What are you doing, Balls?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the puzzle the solver is working on right now
second meaning: an angry exclamation, an irritable word

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an exasperated question ending in an expletive. The answer splits as cross word: 'Balls!' is a cross word, and you are doing a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver is at this moment completing a grid puzzle, and a rude exclamation of annoyance is an angry utterance.

clue.text: Small dramatic role "was orgasmic, love!"

parts.note: came is slang for reached orgasm
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor recalls an ecstatic performance, gushing 'darling!'
explanation.walkthrough: Love here is not an endearment but nil in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance in a film or play, often by a famous performer.

clue.text: see 19ac.
Trump's position regarding White House: "Expose result"

parts.note: having lost the 2020 election, he was out of the presidency
to come out is to be exposed or revealed, the verb supplying its first half

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about Trump's stance on the presidency and a call to reveal the election result.
explanation.walkthrough: Written while Trump was out of office; the colon makes the rest look like a quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence or end product of events, the way things turn out.

clue.text: Bird's looking angry with ballot

parts.note: an angry face turns red
a poll is a vote, a ballot

explanation.surface: Someone is fuming about the way a vote went.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird could be slang for a woman; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The redpoll is a small finch with a red patch on its forehead, a common songbird.
